name: Vegetarian Zhajiangmian
steps: Check that the wheat noodles and both bean pastes contain eggless, animal-derived ingredients or seafood. Pat the tofu dry and dice it into small 1 cm cubes. Finely chop the shiitake mushrooms and onion; mince garlic and ginger. Cut cucumber into thin matchsticks and slice spring onion, keeping both raw toppings chilled.

In a bowl, loosen the yellow soybean paste and sweet bean sauce with 100 ml of the measured water, soy sauce and sugar. Heat 20 ml oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook onion for 3 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook 5–6 minutes until their moisture evaporates and edges brown; add garlic and ginger for the last 1 minute.

Push the vegetables aside, add the remaining 15 ml oil and the tofu cubes, and brown them for 3 minutes without breaking them up. Pour in the bean-paste mixture and remaining 100 ml water. Stir well and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until the sauce is thick, glossy and still spoonable, with visible mushroom and tofu pieces. Taste before adding any extra seasoning because the pastes are salty.

While the sauce simmers, bring the remaining 2000 ml water to a rolling boil. Cook the eggless noodles according to their packet until springy but tender; stir once early to prevent sticking. Drain well and divide among four warm bowls.

Spoon one quarter of the warm brown bean sauce over each bowl of noodles, then arrange a quarter of the cucumber and spring onion on each. Serve immediately so diners can mix the crisp raw vegetables into the hot noodles and sauce themselves.
tips: This is a vegetarian Chinese yellow-soybean-paste version with mushroom and tofu; the Korean dish Jajangmyeon uses a different, much darker chunjang sauce. If the paste is exceptionally salty, thin the finished sauce with a spoonful of noodle water. Keep the cucumber raw for contrast.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
